go advances cursor, clears stopped text and enters running; observe_prompt only promotes connecting/running when fresh tail ends in a full prompt. An unchanged historical prompt no longer permits query or second g. This fixes that normal-flow authorization bug in the offline model.

residual_findings.finding: go marks running before send succeeds; a BrokenPipeError preserves running. execute marks query before send; send/read/process-exit exceptions can preserve query, while only the explicit time deadline becomes unknown. Both were reproduced offline for send failure. State records intent rather than confirmed acceptance on these edges.
residual_findings.minimal_action: Record attempted/sent/fault separately, transition to unknown on local IO/child failures, persist terminal error and last cursor. Treat running only as a continuation request until independent guest response, not proof of execution.

residual_findings.finding: query/unknown intentionally reject later prompts, so timeout recovery cannot automatically clear a breakpoint or resume via the normal API. A fresh late prompt does not fix this state. This fails closed but may leave a paused guest and unresolved owned breakpoint.
residual_findings.minimal_action: Specify a separate bounded recovery handshake with fresh prompt/new marker and explicit current-event validation, or report recovery pending for the owner-controlled external recovery. Never switch to stopped merely from a historical prompt.

residual_findings.finding: collect deadline bounds loop entry, not one synchronous run_guest call. Actual v4 elapsed 29.687 seconds exceeded collect(15). pool.shutdown(wait=True) is also not a hard outer bound. residual_findings.minimal_action: Bound transport receives/retries and overall call; record all started future terminal outcomes in finally without an unbounded wait. Do not infer guest gate time from host monitor duration.

residual_findings.minimal_action: Anchor optional CPU prompt at beginning of a line, tolerate CRLF/chunk boundaries, and test mixed old/new stop blocks plus an exact latest pending break. This is a parser strictness finding, not an observed native failure.

canonical57_blockers: No current target capture exists. The PDB-derived Context pointer at PRCB+0x8980, embedded ContextFrame, user syscall trap, and WOW64 save block are different sources; none may be silently treated as a complete user postreturn CPU.

Fixed kernel KeContextFromKframes normalizes DS/ES/FS/GS and skips current x87 FXSAVE on the inspected kernel-CS debug path. FLOAT context flag or rF output is not proof of a valid x87 header/register image. Missing FIP/FDP/FCS/FDS/FOP and physical-tag/order validity cannot be filled with zero.

SpecialRegisters save writes LDTR zero on the inspected route and conditionally captures descriptors; descriptor bases require full width and hidden caches are not guaranteed by descriptor-table bytes. DR4/5 lack independent storage and CR4.DE determines alias/exception semantics; hardware ba and #DB already alter debug state.

Kernel wait-tail GPRs are not x86 postreturn state. Original trap RAX is not live return status, conditional trap fields need branch validity, and kernel SYSRET path changes registers/MXCSR before WOW64 restores selected saved values.

No dynamic continuous SYSRET/64-to-32 WOW64 branch trace has bound the restored registers, x87/FX state, user return PC and original resources. The saved WOW64 block is a candidate with provenance/validity obligations, not automatic fullstate.

All fixed original-byte excerpts and precise minimal raw-read addresses remain in the separately hashed raw-context contract; this review neither changes that contract nor relaxes complete canonical57, ABI, replay, fresh-lifetime or original-game requirements.
